title: AI 视频 Agent + Skill + Codex : Seedance2.5 即将接入｜用Cod操控的项目级 AI 视频创作实操教学，打通剧本、分镜、成片
text:
Making A I video?
Tired of switching tools and uploading refs over and over?
Flova might just be for you!
It is a project level A I video agent.
it can call upon skills to advance creation.
it can also use Codex to take over the entire process.
Here is a short film I made with Flova and Codex
using just a few prompts,
today, I will show you exactly how to do it.
Before we dive in,
let us clear up the A I video workflow
and a few core concepts,
in a traditional workflow,
common tools have very distinct roles.
Platforms like Kling and Jimeng chiefly generate video clips,
while G P T, NanoBanana, and Suno
round out assets like images and music.
and finally, use tools like CapCut to finish the edit
and piece it all together.
Each tool is mighty,
but once a project gets complex,
character storyboards, asset versions, and revision logs
still fall to the creator
to piece together.
Project level agents tackle this very layer
they do not just generate content,
they manage the entire project,
keeping various models and assets moving forward
within a single workflow.
When using Flova,
a few concepts and tools come into play, first,
the agent handles grasping goals,
breaking down tasks,
calling tools, and moving the process forward.
A skill, then, is a reusable set of production methods
that tells the agent the order of tasks
and which nodes need approval.
Codex is Open A I’s code A I Agent
that can grasp natural language,
run commands, and call upon external tools.
here, we use it as an external agent
to call F L O V A and advance the entire video project.
company
C L I stands for Command Line Interface
in this context, it is the terminal entry point Codex
uses to access and operate Flova.
Simply put, with Flova,
you can either operate it directly within the platform
which is more intuitive
or hand it off to Codex to drive it externally,
which suits automated handling of complex projects better.
Now, let us see it in action!
First, head to the Flova homepage
there, you will find recommended skills of various types,
the community offers even more options,
letting you check out their suited scenarios,
models used, and the specific workflow.
Using a skill is not about learning
how to generate certain visuals,
it is about directly tapping into a set of proven
creative workflows
to help us craft brand new video content.
If you are unsure what to pick at first,
you can just chat with the agent in natural language
right within the dialogue box.
Let it first grasp your needs, sort out tasks,
then match the right skill for the ensuing creative process.
Once the chat kicks off, any generated assets,
storyboards, and video clips
get gathered in the project interface
for you to preview anytime.
If you are not happy midway, you can tweak things via chat,
or hop into the relevant module
to fine tune your project manually.
You can switch between list or canvas view
based on your habits,
which makes viewing and organizing much handier.
So, that covers the platform’s basic usage.
Next up, let us try using Codex to call Flova
and generate a full short film.
First, per the official site’s guide,
copy the prompt,
install the C L I and skill,
then you can call Flova right within Codex via chat.
Here, I have prepped a test prompt
that asks it to create a video project
and check with me at key points.
Once you send the prompt,
Codex will first use the Flova skill to draft a project plan
and have us confirm a few key items.
Confirm no issues, reply continue.
Next, Flova starts generating reference images.
Let us click and take a look
you can see
it not only generated three views of the two leads,
but also created the story’s key elements
and scenes alongside them.
You can tweak it here, but this version looks fine,
so let us move on.
Back in Codex, send continue,
and it will generate six storyboarding keyframes
based on the approved character and scene art.
Skim through them,
and once all looks good, move to the next step.
Send a message in C O D E X to have F L O V
A generate video clips.
Once done, check it out.
The overall effect is quite polished,
and just like with Flova itself,
you can make edits in sync right here.
Once the content's confirmed,
it is on to the final video synthesis
comprising scoring and editing.
Here, Flova generated three B G M tracks.
This one feels too laid back
let us add some tension.
After regenerating, it sounds much more fitting.
Lastly, Codex exports it right here—
and boom, a simple A I video is done!
If you are not happy, you can tweak it again.
from story design to locking in visuals,
with no need to hop between tools.
from keyframes to video generation,
with no need to re specify settings
even B G M and editing are all linked in
all your needs met here,
all in one spot!
Plus, Flova has already brought together many leading models
for image, video, and music,
which it can flexibly call upon for tasks,
Seedance two point five will also launch on Flova soon.
Lastly, let us view the full clip we generated!
This video covers A I Agent for A I video creation.
This year, you can feel it,
before, we were debating
which large language model was smarter,
now, the focus has shifted
everyone is talking about A I Agent s.
An A I Agent is like a large language model
that has grown hands and feet
no longer just a chatbot,
but one that can autonomously carry out entire tasks.
So, this  Complete Guide to A I Agent Tools?
I think it is well worth a favorite!
It is not about one single tool,
rather, it tells you one thing,
A I Agent s are starting to specialize.
For instance, General A I Agent think of it as an all rounder
that can dabble in research, office work,
data processing, and web tasks across various fields.
Moving on, we get to the really useful bits.
For devs, there is the M C P ecosystem
that links up with G I T H U B and Playwright,
for knowledge bases,
you have Vector Database and retrieval platform,
and for no code setup,
you have platforms like Coze and F A S T T.
Many folks now are not writing agents from scratch,
but piecing them together.
Looking further on, it is more akin
to a division of roles by job
some folks focus on writing, others on images and video.
and others focus on vertical niches like academia, law,
healthcare, and finance.
So, A I today is not one catch all button,
but more and more like a toolbox.
You need to know which scenarios call for which tool combos
best suited to your current task.
